items.stem: Mei Ling was so ______ about the school camp that she could not stop smiling.

explain.why: 'bored' means uninterested; someone who cannot stop smiling is not bored
'furious' means very angry; it does not fit with smiling
'ashamed' means embarrassed by wrongdoing; nothing in the sentence suggests this

solution: 'excited' means full of happy anticipation, which matches the constant smiling.

items.stem: The soup tasted so ______ that Dad stirred in a spoonful of salt.

explain.why: 'crunchy' describes a hard, noisy texture; soup is not crunchy
'spicy' means hot with chilli; salt would not be added to fix a spicy soup
'sour' means sharp like lemon; salt is not the usual remedy

solution: 'bland' means lacking flavour, so adding salt makes sense.

items.stem: The kitten ______ after the rolling ball as fast as its tiny legs could carry it.

explain.why: 'trudged' means walked slowly and wearily, the opposite of 'as fast as'
'strolled' means walked in a relaxed way, not at top speed
'crept' means moved quietly and slowly; the kitten is chasing a ball

solution: 'dashed' means ran quickly, matching 'as fast as its tiny legs could carry it'.

items.stem: The thief ______ past the sleeping guard on tiptoe.

explain.why: 'stomped' means walked with heavy noisy steps, the opposite of tiptoeing
'marched' means walked in a stiff, firm rhythm; a thief would not do this past a guard
'ran' means moved fast on foot, which does not match tiptoeing

solution: 'crept' means moved quietly and carefully, as the thief does on tiptoe.

items.stem: The ______ child refused to share her toys with anyone.

explain.why: 'generous' means happy to give; it is the opposite of refusing to share
'polite' means well-mannered; refusing to share is not what makes a child polite
'cheerful' means happy; it does not explain the refusal to share

solution: 'selfish' means caring only about oneself.

items.stem: Grandpa spoke ______ so that even the people at the back of the hall could hear him.

explain.why: 'softly' means in a quiet voice, which would make it harder for the back rows to hear
'shyly' describes a nervous manner, not how loud the voice is
'sleepily' means in a drowsy way; it would not help the back rows to hear

solution: 'loudly' means at high volume, so everyone can hear.

items.stem: The ______ weather forced the school to cancel the picnic.

explain.why: 'pleasant' means nice; nice weather would not cancel a picnic
'sunny' weather is good for a picnic, not a reason to cancel it
'calm' weather has little wind or rain, so there would be no need to cancel

solution: 'stormy' weather with heavy rain and wind is a reason to cancel a picnic.
items.gloss: stormy = with strong wind and rain

items.stem: The puppy wagged its tail ______ when its owner came home.

explain.why: 'sadly' means unhappily; a wagging tail shows the opposite
'angrily' means in an angry way; a dog greeting its owner with a wagging tail is not angry
'fearfully' means in a scared way; it does not fit a happy greeting

solution: A wagging tail on seeing its owner shows the puppy is happy.

items.stem: After running the race, the boys were so ______ that they fell asleep on the bus.

explain.why: 'energetic' means full of energy; it would not lead to falling asleep
'curious' means eager to know something; it does not cause sleep
'thrilled' means very excited; excitement would keep them awake

solution: 'exhausted' means extremely tired, which explains falling asleep.

items.stem: Aisha's room was so ______ that she could not find her shoes.

explain.why: 'spotless' means perfectly clean; she would find her shoes easily
'tidy' means neat; in a tidy room things are easy to find
'spacious' means having lots of room; it does not explain why things are lost

solution: 'messy' means untidy, so things are hard to find.

items.stem: The librarian asked us to speak ______ so that we would not disturb the readers.

explain.why: 'angrily' describes mood, not volume, and would not help avoid disturbance
'loudly' would disturb the readers
'quickly' is about speed; it does not prevent noise

solution: 'quietly' means without much noise, which avoids disturbing readers.

items.stem: Kumar felt ______ when he realised he had lost his wallet.

explain.why: 'delighted' means very pleased; losing a wallet is not a happy event
'amused' means finding something funny; not a natural reaction to a loss
'proud' means pleased with an achievement; it does not fit a loss

solution: 'worried' means anxious, a natural reaction to losing a wallet.

items.stem: The ______ boy answered every question in the quiz correctly.

explain.why: 'foolish' means lacking sense; it contradicts getting every answer right
'sleepy' describes tiredness, not ability
'clumsy' means awkward in movement, not related to answering questions

solution: 'clever' means quick to learn and understand.

items.stem: The baby ______ loudly when she dropped her ice cream.

explain.why: 'laughed' does not fit the sad event of dropping ice cream
'whispered' is the opposite of 'loudly'; babies do not whisper
'sang' does not match a reaction to losing ice cream

solution: A baby loses her ice cream and cries loudly.

items.stem: The bus was so ______ that many passengers had to stand.

explain.why: 'empty' means with nobody inside; then there would be seats for all
'quiet' is about noise, not number of people
'spacious' means with plenty of room, so passengers would not need to stand

solution: 'crowded' means full of people, so there were no seats left.

items.stem: Mum ______ the carrots into small pieces for the stew.

explain.why: you pour liquids, not solid carrots
'stirred' means mixed round with a spoon; it does not make pieces
'boiled' means cooked in hot water; it does not cut the carrots

solution: 'chopped' means cut into pieces.

items.stem: It is ______ to cross the road without looking both ways.

explain.why: 'enjoyable' means pleasant, which does not describe a risk
'pleasant' means nice, not what crossing without looking is
'tiring' means causing tiredness, not risk

solution: 'dangerous' means likely to cause harm.

items.stem: The old man walked ______ with the help of a walking stick.

explain.why: 'speedily' means quickly; a man needing a stick would not walk so
'fast' means quickly, which does not suit an old man who needs a stick
'brightly' goes with light or smiles, not with walking

solution: 'slowly' fits an old man who needs a stick.

items.stem: Ben felt ______ of his sister for winning the first prize.

explain.why: 'afraid of' means scared of; winning a prize gives no reason to fear her
'ashamed' means embarrassed; winning a prize is not shameful
'tired of' means fed up with, which does not fit winning a prize

solution: 'proud of' means pleased about someone's achievement.

items.stem: The test was so ______ that most pupils finished it early.

explain.why: a difficult test would take longer, not shorter
a confusing test would slow pupils down
'hard' means difficult, so most pupils would not finish early

solution: An 'easy' test lets pupils finish early.

items.stem: The fireman ______ the child from the burning house.

explain.why: firemen do not ignore a child in danger
'blamed' means said it was someone's fault; it does not describe getting the child out
'delayed' means made late; it does not describe saving the child

solution: 'rescued' means saved from danger.

items.stem: I am ______ to my teacher for her help with my spelling.

explain.why: 'angry' does not fit being helped
'ungrateful' means not thankful, the opposite of what help deserves
'afraid' means scared, which does not fit being helped

solution: 'grateful to' means thankful to someone.

items.stem: The ______ of the jungle made the children feel afraid.

explain.why: brightness would make them feel safer
'warmth' suggests comfort, not fear
'cheer' means happiness, not a cause of fear

solution: Darkness in a jungle is a natural cause of fear.

items.stem: Our class ______ money to help the flood victims.

explain.why: 'squandered' means wasted; it does not match helping the victims
'stole' means took without permission, not how a class helps victims
'borrowed' means took to give back; it does not help victims

solution: 'collected' means gathered together money to give.

items.stem: The ______ puppy hid under the bed when it heard the fireworks.

explain.why: 'mischievous' means playfully naughty; hiding from noise is not that
'hungry' does not explain hiding from noise
'proud' does not match hiding

solution: Hiding from loud noise shows the puppy is 'frightened'.

items.stem: Although she had won the debate, Priya remained ______ and thanked her teammates for the credit.

explain.why: 'vain' means too proud of oneself; she gives credit to others
'arrogant' means showing too much self-importance; she thanks others instead
'stubborn' means refusing to change one's mind; it is not about humility

solution: 'modest' means not boasting about one's success.

items.stem: The ______ aroma of curry drifted from the hawker stall and made our stomachs growl.

explain.why: 'revolting' means disgusting; it would not make stomachs growl
'unpleasant' would not make stomachs growl
'stale' means no longer fresh; a stale smell would not make people hungry

solution: 'appetising' means making people want to eat.

items.stem: The twins looked ______ alike that even their teacher mixed them up.

explain.why: 'rarely' means not often; it describes frequency, not degree
'hardly alike' means barely alike, which would not cause a mix-up
'moderately' means to a medium degree, too weak to explain the mix-up

solution: 'remarkably alike' means extremely alike, which explains the mix-up.

items.stem: The shopkeeper ______ the customer of trying to steal a packet of biscuits.

explain.why: you 'blame someone for' something, not 'blame someone of' it
you 'scold someone for' something; 'of' does not follow
'warned someone of' needs a danger, not a wrongdoing he is said to have done

solution: 'accused someone of' is the correct collocation for saying someone did wrong.
items.gloss: accuse of = say someone did wrong

items.stem: The students listened ______ as the astronaut described her trip to space.

explain.why: 'inattentively' means without paying attention, the opposite of the sentence
'grudgingly' means unwillingly, which does not fit a fascinating talk
'idly' means without purpose; it suggests not really listening

solution: 'attentively' means paying close attention.

items.stem: My brother is very ______; he never wastes a single cent on things he does not need.

explain.why: 'extravagant' means spending too much, the opposite of never wasting money
'lavish' means spending freely, the opposite of never wasting a cent
'careless' means not taking care, which does not describe money habits here

solution: 'thrifty' means careful with money.

items.stem: The sudden clap of thunder ______ the baby, who began to cry.

explain.why: 'amused' means entertained; a baby who cries is not amused
'soothed' means calmed; the baby began to cry
'entertained' means amused, but the baby cried

solution: 'startled' means gave a sudden shock.

items.stem: The detective examined the room ______, not missing even a single footprint.

explain.why: 'superficially' means only on the surface, so he would miss details
'casually' means without much attention; it contradicts not missing a footprint
'lazily' means without effort; it contradicts the thorough search

solution: 'meticulously' means with great care about details.

items.stem: Despite the heavy rain, the runners ______ in finishing the race.

explain.why: 'insisted' goes with 'on', not 'in'
'resisted' means fought against; it does not fit finishing a race
'consisted' says what something is made of; it does not mean kept going

solution: 'persisted in' means kept going despite difficulty.

items.stem: The principal's speech was so ______ that several pupils began to yawn.

explain.why: 'thrilling' means very exciting, which would not cause yawning
'amusing' means funny, which keeps people awake
'inspiring' means encouraging, which would hold attention

solution: 'tedious' means long and boring, causing yawns.

items.stem: Rina felt ______ when her friends forgot her birthday.

explain.why: 'thrilled' means very excited; forgotten birthdays do not cause this
'determined' means set on doing something; unrelated to being forgotten
'curious' means eager to learn; it is not the feeling of being forgotten

solution: 'neglected' means feeling ignored or unimportant.

items.stem: The wooden hut was so ______ that a strong wind could have blown it down.

explain.why: 'sturdy' means strong, so wind could not blow it down
'spacious' is about size, not strength
'ancient' means very old; old things may be strong, so it does not give the result

solution: 'flimsy' means weak and easily damaged.

items.stem: The ______ shopkeeper gave the lost child a sweet and called her mother.

explain.why: 'unsympathetic' means not feeling for others, but she helped the child
'hostile' means unfriendly; she was kind to the child
'impatient' means unwilling to wait; she took time to help

solution: 'compassionate' means showing kindness to someone in trouble.

items.stem: The fruit seller ______ the apples carefully so that they would not bruise.

explain.why: 'hurled' means threw hard, which would bruise apples
'dumped' means dropped carelessly, which would bruise apples
'scattered' means thrown about, which would not be careful

solution: 'arranged' means put in order with care.

items.stem: The accountant ______ the figures twice to make sure there were no mistakes.

explain.why: 'invented' means made up, which would be dishonest here
'ignored' means paid no attention, the opposite of making sure
'guessed' means estimated without checking, the opposite of making sure

solution: 'verified' means checked to be correct.
items.gloss: verify = check that something is true

items.stem: The ______ trail was full of rocks and tree roots, so the hikers moved slowly.

explain.why: 'smooth' means even; rocks and roots make a path uneven
'tidy' means neat; it does not describe a rocky path
'flat' means level; rocks and roots make it uneven

solution: 'rugged' means rough and uneven.

items.stem: The boy ______ the secret to his best friend in a low voice.

explain.why: 'shouted' means said very loudly, not 'in a low voice'
'announced' means said publicly; a secret is not announced
'declared' means stated firmly and openly, not a quiet secret

solution: 'whispered' means spoke very softly, matching 'in a low voice'.

items.stem: Mrs Tan was ______ with the class's progress and gave everyone a sticker.

explain.why: 'puzzled' means confused; it would not lead to a reward
'startled' means shocked, not a reason for a reward
'displeased' means not happy; she gave stickers as a reward

solution: 'delighted' means very pleased.

items.stem: The stray dog looked ______, its ribs showing under its dull coat.

explain.why: 'plump' means rounded and well fed; visible ribs show the opposite
'sleek' means smooth and glossy, which does not fit a dull coat
'muscular' means strongly built; visible ribs show thinness

solution: 'scrawny' means thin and underfed.

items.stem: Uncle Lim is famous for his ______ service; he never keeps customers waiting.

explain.why: 'sluggish' means slow, the opposite of never keeping customers waiting
'casual' means relaxed; it says nothing about speed
'grudging' means unwilling, which does not describe quick service

solution: 'prompt' means quick and on time.

items.stem: The two brothers were ______ over who should wash the dishes.

explain.why: 'chatting' means talking in a friendly way; it does not fit a dispute
'rejoicing' means celebrating, which is odd for chores
'whispering' means speaking softly, which does not show a dispute

solution: 'bickering' means arguing about small matters.

items.stem: The magician's trick ______ the audience, who could not guess how it was done.

explain.why: 'bored' means uninterested; people trying to guess are interested
'scolded' means told off; a trick does not scold
'flattered' means praised too much; it does not explain not guessing

solution: 'baffled' means completely puzzled.

items.stem: She spoke ______ about her dream of becoming a doctor, her eyes shining.

explain.why: 'reluctantly' means unwillingly; shining eyes show enthusiasm
'nervously' means with fear; shining eyes suggest joy
'indifferently' means without interest, the opposite of shining eyes

solution: 'passionately' means with strong feeling.

items.stem: The athlete's ______ determination inspired the whole team.

explain.why: 'temporary' means lasting a short time; it could not inspire a team
'hesitant' means unsure, the opposite of firm determination
'inconsistent' means changing, which would not inspire a team

solution: 'unwavering' means steady and never weakening.

items.stem: The match was ______ until Saturday because of the rain.

explain.why: a match 'cancelled until' a date is wrong; cancelled means it will not happen
'ended until Saturday' makes no sense
'repeated' means done again, but the match had not yet been played

solution: 'postponed until' means moved to a later time.
items.gloss: postpone = move to a later time

items.stem: The minister's ______ remarks about the new policy left reporters unsure whether he supported it.

explain.why: 'forthright' means direct and honest, so reporters would know his view
'hostile' means unfriendly; it does not explain the uncertainty
'emphatic' means forceful and clear, the opposite of leaving people unsure

solution: 'ambiguous' means open to more than one meaning.

items.stem: Her ______ curiosity led her to open every drawer and cupboard in the house.

explain.why: 'fleeting' means short-lived, which would not drive such thorough searching
'halfhearted' means without enthusiasm, the opposite of opening every drawer
'dormant' means inactive, the opposite of her restless searching

solution: 'insatiable' means impossible to satisfy.

items.stem: He gave a ______ shrug, as if the outcome of the match made no difference to him.

explain.why: 'bewildered' means confused, not unconcerned
'ecstatic' means overjoyed, which does not fit 'no difference'
'sheepish' means embarrassed; it does not mean unconcerned

solution: 'nonchalant' means calm and unconcerned.

items.stem: The scientist's findings were ______ by later experiments, which proved her theory correct.

explain.why: 'contradicted' means said the opposite, but the experiments proved her correct
'overlooked' means not noticed; later experiments could not prove her theory by being unseen
'postponed' goes with events, not findings

solution: 'corroborated' means supported with further evidence.

items.stem: The ______ child clung to her mother's skirt and refused to greet the guests.

explain.why: 'mischievous' means playfully naughty; it does not explain clinging
'bold' means confident, the opposite of clinging and refusing to greet
'inquisitive' means eager to learn; it does not explain refusing to greet

solution: 'timid' means shy and easily frightened.

items.stem: After weeks of ______ practice, she finally played the piece without a single error.

explain.why: 'sporadic' means happening now and then, which rarely produces faultless playing
'casual' means relaxed and not serious, too weak to explain a perfect result
'halfhearted' means without enthusiasm, unlikely to give perfect results

solution: 'diligent' means careful and hardworking, which explains the result.

items.stem: The manager's ______ tone calmed the angry customers.

explain.why: 'sarcastic' means mocking, which would anger them more
'curt' means rudely brief, which would make them angrier
'patronising' means talking down, which would annoy them more

solution: 'soothing' means calming.

items.stem: Ali's excuse was so ______ that no one believed it for a moment.

explain.why: 'trustworthy' describes a person, and a trustworthy excuse would be believed
a genuine excuse would be true and believed
a convincing excuse would persuade people

solution: 'implausible' means hard to believe.

items.stem: The mountaineers had to ______ the dangerous slope before dawn, while the snow was still hard.

explain.why: you transfer objects or people, not a slope
you transport goods; you do not 'transport a slope'
'transmit' means send a signal or illness, not cross a place

solution: 'traverse' means to cross.

items.stem: She was ______ to admit her mistake, even though everyone had already noticed it.

explain.why: 'eager' means keen, the opposite of 'even though'
'delighted' means very pleased; people are not pleased to admit a mistake
'proud' does not fit a mistake that she is hiding

solution: 'reluctant' means unwilling, which fits 'even though everyone had noticed'.

items.stem: The old fisherman had a ______ face, lined by years of sun and wind.

explain.why: 'immaculate' means perfectly clean and neat, not lined by wind
'pampered' means spoiled with care, not worn by weather
'glossy' means smooth and shiny, not lined

solution: 'weathered' means worn by exposure to weather.

items.stem: The headmaster's stern warning had a ______ effect on the noisy class; not a whisper was heard.

explain.why: 'soothing' means comforting; a stern warning does not comfort
'amusing' means funny, which would not silence a class
'refreshing' means pleasantly new or cooling, which does not fit

solution: 'sobering' means making someone serious.

items.stem: The villagers lived in ______ conditions, with no clean water and barely enough food.

explain.why: 'comfortable' means having ease, the opposite of having no water
'prosperous' means wealthy, which contradicts lacking food
'ample' means plenty, but there is barely enough

solution: 'wretched' means miserable and poor.

items.stem: The tourists were ______ by the grandeur of the ancient temple and fell silent.

explain.why: 'amused' means entertained; it does not explain falling silent
'irritated' means annoyed, which does not suit admiring grandeur
'embarrassed' means feeling awkward, which grandeur does not cause

solution: 'overawed' means filled with wonder.

items.stem: His ______ remarks about her cooking made Mei lose her appetite.

explain.why: 'complimentary' means praising, which would please her
'enthusiastic' means very keen, which would not hurt her
'tentative' means uncertain; it does not explain her lost appetite

solution: 'disparaging' means speaking of something as having little value.

items.stem: The company's profits ______ sharply after the new product was launched.

explain.why: 'paused' means stopped for a while, not rose 'sharply'
'lingered' means stayed behind, not rose quickly
'wandered' means moved without aim, unsuited to profits rising

solution: 'soared' means rose rapidly.

items.stem: The librarian's ______ gaze made the noisy boys fall silent at once.

explain.why: 'wistful' means sadly longing, which would not silence boys
a 'kind' gaze would not make noisy boys fall silent
'admiring' means full of praise, which would not silence them

solution: 'stern' means serious and strict.

items.stem: The speaker tried to ______ the angry crowd with a calm and polite reply.

explain.why: 'provoke' means make angrier, which a calm reply would not do
'ignore' does not fit 'with a calm and polite reply', which is a response
'inflame' means make angrier, the opposite of calm

solution: 'pacify' means calm someone down.

items.stem: Encouraged by the latest trial, the scientists are ______ that a cure will be found within ten years.

explain.why: 'pessimistic' means expecting the worst; 'encouraged' points to hope
'sceptical' means doubtful; being encouraged does not make people doubtful
'indifferent' means not caring; the scientists are working on a cure and are encouraged

solution: 'optimistic' means hopeful about the future.

items.stem: The refugees were ______ with food and blankets by the volunteers.

explain.why: you donate things, not 'donate people with' things; the pattern 'were donated with' is wrong
'contributed' is not used with 'with' in this way
'granted' goes with permission or wishes, and not with 'with food'

solution: 'provided with' is the right pattern for 'given what is needed'.

items.stem: Mr Lee is a ______ man who rarely says more than he needs to.

explain.why: 'talkative' means chatty, the opposite of rarely speaking
'outspoken' means frank in speaking out, the opposite of rarely speaking
'sociable' means fond of company, which does not fit someone who says little

solution: 'reserved' means quiet and slow to show feelings.

items.stem: The explorers had to ______ on fish and wild fruit to stay alive.

explain.why: 'insist on' means demand; it does not mean survive on food
'persist in' means keep going, not live on food
'consist of' is used for things made of parts, not people staying alive

solution: 'subsist on' means stay alive on little food.

items.stem: The toddler was ______ by the colourful bubbles and could not look away.

explain.why: 'unnerved' means made nervous, which would make her look away
'disheartened' means discouraged, which would not hold a toddler's gaze
'deterred' means put off, the opposite of not looking away

solution: 'mesmerised' means held completely in attention.

items.stem: The singer's ______ voice filled the hall and brought tears to many eyes.

explain.why: 'monotonous' means dull and unchanging, which would not bring tears
'feeble' means weak, which would not fill a hall
'hoarse' means rough from a sore throat, which does not bring tears

solution: 'haunting' means beautiful in a sad, lingering way.

items.stem: The teacher was ______ with first-time offenders, giving them a warning rather than a detention.

explain.why: 'ruthless' means without pity, the opposite of giving a warning
'furious' means very angry, which does not fit a mere warning
'indifferent' means not caring; she did give a warning

solution: 'lenient' means not strict in punishing.
